source_text:
ἑκουσιάζεσθαί τινας, τουτέστι προσκομίζειν Θεῷ· τὰ ἑκούσια δὲ ταῦτα ἦσαν· τὰ ὑπὲρ τὸν
νόμον, ὡς ἐξ ἀγαθῆς καὶ φιλοθέον φιλοτιμίας καρποί· ἀλλ' ἦν μὲν οὐ θέμις τῶν ἐν
νόμῳ διατεταγμένων ῥᾳθυμῆσαι θυσιῶν· ἐπαίνου γεμὴν ἀξίους ἡγεῖτο Θεὸς τοὺς
προστιθέντας ἐκείνοις τὰ οἴκοθέν τε καὶ ἀπὸ γνώμης ἰδίας. τοῦτό τι καὶ νῦν
ἐξῳκονομῆσθαί φαμεν· οὐκ ἀπέφησε μὲν γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς τὸ εἴπερ τις ἕλοιτο καὶ τῆς κατὰ
νόμον ἅπτεσθαι κοινωνίας· κατορθοῦν δὲ τὸ μεῖζον ἡμᾶς ἀπείρξειεν ἂν οὐδὲν, εἰ τῆς εἰς
λῆξιν εὐκλείας μεταποιεῖσθαι σπουδάζομεν. ἄριστα οὖν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει μὲν τοῖς
ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ· τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσι
παραγγέλλω οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλ' ὁ Κύριος, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· παρακομίζει δὲ εἰς ὑποτύπωσιν τῆς
ἐξειλεγμένης καὶ ἀπερισπάστου ζωῆς τὰ καθ' ἑαυτὸν, πάντως που τὴν ἀγαμίαν τοῦ
ἑτέρου προθείς. οὐκοῦν εἰ καὶ ἀπεδύσατό τις τὸν τοῦ νόμου ζυγὸν, μενέτω φησὶν ἐν
ἐγκρατείᾳ· κληρονομήσει γὰρ οὕτω τὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείαν. καὶ πιστώσεται λέγων
ὁ τῶν στεφάνων διανομεύς "Τάδε λέγει Κύριος τοῖς εὐνούχοις 270 "Ὅσοι ἂν
φυλάζωνται τὰ σάββατά μου καὶ ἐκλέξωνται ἃ "ἐγὼ θέλω καὶ ἀντέχωνται τῆς διαθήκης
μου, δώσω αὐτοῖς "ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου καὶ ἐν τῷ τείχει μου τόπον ὀνομαστὸν, "κρεῖσσον
υἱῶν καὶ θυγατέρων ὄνομα αἰώνιον δώσω αὐτοῖς "καὶ οὐκ ἐκλείψει." Οὐκοῦν τῆς
ἐγκρατείας ἀξιόληπτος ὁ μισθός· τοῖς γεμὴν ἤδη τῷ γάμῳ κατειλημμένοις, ἀποφοιτᾶν
οὐκ ἀφίησι τῆς ἅπαξ συνῳκισμένης, ἵνα μὴ θορύβων ἔμπλεων τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν τὸ
σωτήριον ἀποφήνῃ κήρυγμα· οὐκ ἐπαινοῦντος τὸ χρῆμα τοῦ πάντων ἡμῶν Σωτῆρος
Χριστοῦ, εἰ καὶ ὁ νόμος οἰκονομικῶς ἐφῆκε τοῖς ἀρχαιοτέροις τοῦτο ποιεῖν διὰ "τὴν
"σκληροκαρδίαν αὐτῶν," καθά φησιν αὐτὸς ὁ Σωτήρ.
Ὅτι δὲ ἀσφαλέστεροί τε καὶ ἀλκιμώτεροι τῶν ἀρχαιοτέρων οἱ ἐν Χριστῷ,
κἀντεῦθεν ἰδεῖν τοῖς ἐθέλουσι ῥᾷον· ὁ μὲν γὰρ νόμος τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ ἀπέφησε τὸ δεῖν
ἀλλοφύλοις συνιέναι τε καὶ γαμικῶς ἀναπλέκεσθαι· ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς
γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. ἐκείνοις μὲν γὰρ ὁ νοῦς ἦν σαθρὸς καὶ σεσαλευμένος,
ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως· κεχρίσμεθα γὰρ εἰς υἱοθεσίαν τῷ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι καὶ κατῴκηκεν ἐν
ἡμῖν ὁ Χριστός· βεβηκότες δὴ οὖν οὕτως πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἀγαθῶν, δεδίαμεν κατ'
οὐδένα τρόπον τὸ συνεῖναί τινι τῶν ἀπίστων ἔτι· τεθαῤῥήκαμεν δὲ μᾶλλον ὅτι
σαγηνεύσομεν εἰς εὐσέβειαν, καὶ οὐχ ἡμεῖς τῆς ἐνούσης ἐκείνοις ἀμαθίας ἐσόμεθα
θήραμα· καὶ εὐλογοῦμεν μᾶλλον τοὺς οὔπω πιστεύσαντας ἢ μολυνόμεθα παρ' αὐτῶν·
ἡγίασται γάρ φησιν ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί· οὕτως 271 εἰσὶν ἅγια καὶ τὰ τέκνα
ὑμῶν, νικῶντος πάντως που τοῦ ἐν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἁγιασμοῦ τῶν οὔπω
πεπιστευκότων τὸν ῥύπον. εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεταί φησιν, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται
ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις· οἰχέσθω γὰρ, εἰ δοκεῖ, τοῦ ἁγιάζοντος ὁ
μεμολυσμένος, γνώμης ἰδίας ὀψώνιον ἔχων τὴν ἔν γε τούτῳ ζημίαν· ἀνυπαίτιος δὲ
παντελῶς ὁ ταῖς θείαις ἑπόμενος ἐντολαῖς· εὐλογηθήσεται γὰρ ὡς εὐήνιος παρὰ τοῦ
πάντων ἡμῶν Σωτῆρος Χριστοῦ. Περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ ἐπισπάσθω· ἐν
ἀκροβυστίᾳ τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ περιτεμνέσθω. Τινὲς ὡς εἰκὸς τῶν ἐκ περιτομῆς
διελογίζοντο καθ' ἑαυτούς Πῶς ἐσόμεθα δεκτοὶ καὶ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ζωὴν τιμήσομεν,
ἔχοντες ἤδη τὴν περιτομήν; δεήσει τάχα που καὶ 272 ἐπισπᾶσθαι, τουτέστι παλινδρομεῖν
εἰς ἀκροβυστίαν, καὶ τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καταβιάζεσθαι φύσιν· οἱ γεμὴν ἐξ ἑλληνικῆς
ἐρχόμενοι πλάνης, παρὰ τῶν ἔτι τὴν ἐν νόμῳ τιμώντων σκιὰν τάχα που μανθάνοντες,
ὡς ἔστι χρῆμα τίμιον ἡ περιτομὴ, καὶ πᾶσιν ἁγίοις τετηρημένον, καίτοι τὴν πίστιν ἔσθ'
pass_a_gloss: [continues from u02-rem-close: 'it permitted besides these also'] some to make freewill offerings (ἑκουσιάζομαι), that is, to bring (προσκομίζω) to God; and these were the freewill [offerings] (ἑκούσια): the things beyond (ὑπέρ) the law, as fruits (καρπός) of a good and God-loving (φιλόθεος) generosity/ambition (φιλοτιμία); but it was not lawful (θέμις) to be negligent (ῥᾳθυμέω) of the sacrifices ordained (διατάσσω, pf. pass.) in the law; yet God considered (ἡγέομαι) worthy (ἄξιος) of praise (ἔπαινος) those adding (προστίθημι) to those the things from their own home (οἴκοθεν) and from their own judgment (γνώμη). Something of this we say also now has been arranged (ἐξοικονομέω, pf. pass.); for Christ did not forbid (ἀπόφημι) the [case] if someone should choose (αἱρέομαι) also to touch (ἅπτομαι) the fellowship/union (κοινωνία) according to law; but nothing would prevent (ἀπείργω, opt.) us from achieving (κατορθόω) the greater (μείζων), if we are eager (σπουδάζω) to lay claim to (μεταποιέομαι) glory (εὔκλεια) for an allotted portion (λῆξις). Excellently therefore Paul says to the unmarried and the widows, good for them if they remain as I also; but to the married (γαμέω, pf. ptc.) I command (παραγγέλλω), not I but the Lord, and the following; and he brings forward (παρακομίζω) for a pattern (ὑποτύπωσις) of the chosen (ἐκλέγω, pf. ptc.) and undistracted (ἀπερίσπαστος) life his own case, surely setting before (προτίθημι) the other the unmarried state (ἀγαμία). Therefore if someone has stripped off (ἀποδύομαι) the yoke (ζυγός) of the law, let him remain, he says, in self-control (ἐγκράτεια); for thus he will inherit (κληρονομέω) the kingdom of the heavens. And the distributor (διανομεύς) of the crowns (στέφανος) will confirm (πιστόομαι) [it] saying: 'Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs (εὐνοῦχος): Whoever keep (φυλάσσω) my Sabbaths and choose (ἐκλέγομαι) what I will (θέλω) and hold fast (ἀντέχομαι) to my covenant (διαθήκη), I will give them in my house and in my wall (τεῖχος) a named (ὀνομαστός) place, better than sons and daughters; an everlasting (αἰώνιος) name I will give them and it will not fail (ἐκλείπω).' So worth taking (ἀξιόληπτος) [is] the wage (μισθός) of self-control; but those already seized (καταλαμβάνω, pf. pass.) by marriage he does not allow (ἀφίημι) to depart (ἀποφοιτάω) from the one once made to cohabit (συνοικίζω, pf. pass.) [with them], so that the saving (σωτήριος) proclamation may not make (ἀποφαίνω) the [world] under heaven full of tumults (θόρυβος); Christ the Savior of us all not praising (ἐπαινέω) the thing, even if the law by dispensation (οἰκονομικῶς) permitted (ἐφίημι) the more ancient (ἀρχαιότερος) to do this 'because of their hardness of heart (σκληροκαρδία)', as the Savior himself says. And that more secure (ἀσφαλής) and stronger (ἄλκιμος) than the more ancient [are] those in Christ, also from here [it is] easier for those wishing to see; for the law forbade (ἀπόφημι) to those from Israel that they should associate (σύνειμι) with foreigners (ἀλλόφυλος) and be intertwined (ἀναπλέκω) in marriage (γαμικῶς); but to us Paul [says]: If some brother has an unbelieving (ἄπιστος) wife, and the following. For to them the mind was rotten (σαθρός) and shaken (σαλεύω, pf. pass.), but we not so; for we have been anointed (χρίω, pf. pass.) for adoption (υἱοθεσία) with the Holy Spirit and Christ has dwelt in us; being thus set firm (βαίνω, pf. ptc.) toward anything of the good things, we fear (δέδια) in no way to be with (σύνειμι) any of the unbelievers any longer; rather we are confident (θαρρέω, pf.) that we will catch in a dragnet (σαγηνεύω) into godliness (εὐσέβεια), and that we will not be the prey (θήραμα) of the ignorance (ἀμαθία) in them; and we bless (εὐλογέω) rather those not yet having believed (πιστεύω) than are defiled (μολύνω) by them; for the unbelieving husband, he says, has been sanctified in the wife; so also your children are holy, the sanctification (ἁγιασμός) in those believing surely conquering (νικάω) the filth (ῥύπος) of those not yet having believed. But if the unbeliever separates (χωρίζω), he says, let him separate; the brother or the sister has not been enslaved (δουλόω, pf. pass.) in such [cases]; for let the defiled one go off (οἴχομαι, impv.), if it seems [good], from the one sanctifying (ἁγιάζω), having as wages (ὀψώνιον) of his own judgment the loss (ζημία) in this at least; but wholly blameless (ἀνυπαίτιος) the one following (ἕπομαι) the divine commandments; for he will be blessed (εὐλογέω, fut. pass.) as obedient (εὐήνιος) by Christ the Savior of us all. [Lemma:] Was anyone called (καλέω) having been circumcised (περιτέμνω, pf. pass.)? let him not draw over (ἐπισπάομαι); was anyone called in uncircumcision (ἀκροβυστία)? let him not be circumcised. Some, as is likely (εἰκός), of those from the circumcision (περιτομή) were reasoning (διαλογίζομαι) by themselves: How shall we be acceptable (δεκτός) and honor (τιμάω) the life in Christ, having already the circumcision? Perhaps it will be necessary also to draw over, that is, to run back (παλινδρομέω) into uncircumcision, and to force (καταβιάζομαι) the nature of the flesh; but those coming from the Hellenic (ἑλληνικός) error (πλάνη), learning (μανθάνω) perhaps from those still honoring the shadow (σκιά) in the law that circumcision is a precious (τίμιος) thing and kept (τηρέω, pf. pass.) by all saints, although (καίτοι) the faith (πίστις) some- [block breaks at ἔσθ'; continues in u03-rem-early: ὅτε παραδεξάμενοι, ἐπετελοῦντο σαρκί]
pass_b_english: …some to make freewill offerings, that is, to bring gifts to God. These freewill offerings were the things beyond what the law required, given as the fruits of a good and God-loving generosity. It was not permitted to neglect the sacrifices ordained in the law, but God counted worthy of praise those who added to them gifts of their own, from their own free choice. We say that something of this kind has been arranged now as well. For Christ did not forbid anyone who so chooses to take part in the union the law allows; but nothing would keep us from achieving the greater thing, if we are eager to lay claim to glory as our final portion.

Paul therefore does very well to say to the unmarried and the widows, “It is good for them if they remain as I am” (1 Corinthians 7:8), but, “To the married I give charge, not I but the Lord,” and so on (1 Corinthians 7:10). He brings forward his own case as a pattern of the chosen and undistracted life (compare 1 Corinthians 7:35), plainly ranking the unmarried state above the other. So if anyone has put off the yoke of the law, let him remain, he says, in self-control; for in this way he will inherit the kingdom of heaven. And the One who awards the crowns will confirm it, saying, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: As many as keep my Sabbaths, and choose the things that I will, and hold fast to my covenant, to them I will give in my house and within my wall a renowned place, better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it shall not fail” (Isaiah 56:4–5).

So the reward of self-control is worth the winning. But those already bound by marriage he does not permit to leave the wife once joined to them, so that the message of salvation may not fill the world under heaven with turmoil. For Christ, the Savior of us all, does not approve of this practice, even though the law, by way of concession, allowed the people of old to do it “because of their hardness of heart” (Matthew 19:8), as the Savior himself says.

That those in Christ are steadier and stronger than the people of old, anyone who wishes can easily see from this as well. The law forbade the children of Israel to associate with foreigners and to be bound to them in marriage (compare Deuteronomy 7:3); but to us Paul says, “If any brother has a wife who is an unbeliever,” and so on (1 Corinthians 7:12). For their mind was unsound and unsteady, but we are not so; for we have been anointed with the Holy Spirit for adoption as sons, and Christ has come to dwell in us. Standing so firmly, then, toward every good thing, we are in no way afraid any longer to live with one of the unbelievers. Rather, we are confident that we will draw them as in a net into godliness, and that we will not become the prey of the ignorance that is in them. We bless those who have not yet believed rather than being defiled by them.

For “the unbelieving husband,” he says, “has been made holy in his wife,” and so “your children too are holy” (1 Corinthians 7:14), since the holiness in those who believe surely overcomes the filth of those who have not yet believed. “But if the unbeliever separates,” he says, “let him separate; in such cases the brother or the sister is not enslaved” (1 Corinthians 7:15). Let the defiled one go away, if he so decides, from the one who makes him holy, and take the loss that comes with it as the wages of his own choice. But the one who follows the divine commandments is wholly blameless; for he will be blessed as obedient by Christ, the Savior of us all.
“Was anyone called when already circumcised? Let him not remove the marks of circumcision. Was anyone called while uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised” (1 Corinthians 7:18).

Some of those from the circumcision, it seems, were reasoning among themselves: “How shall we be acceptable and honor the life in Christ, when we already have circumcision? Perhaps we shall have to draw the foreskin forward, that is, to go back to uncircumcision and do violence to the nature of the flesh.” But those who came from pagan error, learning perhaps from those who still honored the shadow in the law that circumcision is a precious thing and one kept by all the saints, although the faith…

choices.why: The LXX term for gifts beyond what the law required.
λῆξις is an allotted portion or inheritance.
Kept literally; the Greek does not narrow it.

choices.english: draw them as in a net

bible_refs.note: λέγει μὲν τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ = 1 Corinthians 7:8.
τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσι παραγγέλλω οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλ' ὁ Κύριος = 1 Corinthians 7:10.
τῆς … ἀπερισπάστου ζωῆς picks up Paul's εὐπάρεδρον τῷ κυρίῳ ἀπερισπάστως in the same chapter.

LXX Isaiah 56:4–5: τάδε λέγει κύριος τοῖς εὐνούχοις ὅσοι ἂν φυλάξωνται τὰ σάββατά μου καὶ ἐκλέξωνται ἃ ἐγὼ θέλω καὶ ἀντέχωνται τῆς διαθήκης μου, δώσω αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου καὶ ἐν τῷ τείχει μου τόπον ὀνομαστὸν κρείττω υἱῶν καὶ θυγατέρων, ὄνομα αἰώνιον δώσω αὐτοῖς καὶ οὐκ ἐκλείψει. The source's φυλάζωνται is an OCR slip for φυλάξωνται.

διὰ τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν αὐτῶν adapts πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν (Matthew 19:8; also Mark 10:5); καθά φησιν αὐτὸς ὁ Σωτήρ marks it as Christ's word. Matthew is cited because Cyril has just quoted Matthew 19.
The law's ban on marriage with foreigners (οὐδὲ μὴ γαμβρεύσητε πρὸς αὐτούς) is summarised, not quoted.
εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον = 1 Corinthians 7:12.
ἡγίασται … ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί = 7:14a; οὕτως εἰσὶν ἅγια καὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν paraphrases 7:14c (νῦν δὲ ἅγιά ἐστιν).
εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις = 1 Corinthians 7:15a.
Lemma: περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ ἐπισπάσθω· ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ περιτεμνέσθω, quoted in full; modern editions read ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ κέκληταί τις in the second clause, Cyril has ἐκλήθη.

notes: Pass A gloss written from the Greek of this row; Pass B checked clause by clause against it (negation, agency, modality, doctrine).
Scripture citations placed beside the clause, full book name and chapter:verse; LXX Psalm numbers converted.

Staged row checked clause by clause against the Greek: faithful, Scripture identified correctly (1 Corinthians 7:8, 7:10, 7:12, 7:14, 7:15, 7:18; Isaiah 56:4–5 LXX; Matthew 19:8). Two small fixes made in tr2.json: γάρ restored ('For Christ did not forbid'), since the clause gives the reason for the analogy; Isaiah 56:4–5 had a number clash ('Whoever keeps … I will give them'); ὅσοι ἂν φυλάξωνται is plural, so now 'As many as keep … to them I will give'.
